new_findings.kind: security (asset gate hides a browser-loaded URL; exact R5/R6 FAIL class: the crate's CSS tokenizer reads bytes differently from a browser's CSS tokenizer before classification)
new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-web/src/cssurl.rs:258-265 (the number arm: `'0'..='9' => { while cur.peek().is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '.') { cur.bump(); } if cur.starts_ident() { cur.ident(); } }`). The same code is at f6e5a49 cssurl.rs:248 and at the R7 PASS commit 08ad0ad, unchanged. Reached from css_references (cssurl.rs:247) via Collector::css (assets.rs:438-450) for both a `style` attribute / SVG presentation attribute (Kind::Css) and a `style` element body (style_children, assets.rs:540-548).
new_findings.evidence:
The number arm consumes EVERY '.' (not only a '.' followed by a digit, contrary to CSS Syntax 3 4.3.3 and the Chromium tokenizer) and then, via `if cur.starts_ident() { cur.ident(); }`, swallows a trailing identifier WITHOUT ever checking for a following '(' - so a `url(` immediately after a number+dot is never recognised as a url function. On its own this only under-recognises one url, but the crate's main loop then treats the bytes after '(' as ordinary CSS, where '/*' opens a comment (cssurl.rs:253 skip_comment) that runs to the next '*/' or to EOF, swallowing any later real url(). Payload (style attribute): `
`. Browser (CSS tokenizer): `1` number, `.` delim, `url("/*")` url token -> declaration `a` is invalid and dropped; the separate declaration `background:url(https://evil.example/p.png)` is valid and the image LOADS. Crate: number arm eats `1.`, ident() eats `url`, main loop bumps `(`, sees `/*` and runs skip_comment to EOF (no `*/`), so css_references returns nothing - collect_assets reports the external URL neither as Denied nor to the port. Same in a ``. Contrast with the existing decoy `1url(` (css_decoys_case_and_whitespace_follow_the_tokenizer, source_dom_patch.rs:1278), which is a dimension token for the browser too and correctly not loaded - no test has a number+DOT before url(, so this hole is unpinned at 62d8983. The difftest comparator models no CSS (its style-sheet-text check compares the TEXT handed to CSS, not the CSS tokenisation), so it cannot see it. No cssurl unit tests exist.
new_findings.remediation: Make the number arm follow CSS Syntax 3 4.3.3: consume a leading/number '.' only when the next code point is a digit (also handle the exponent), and do NOT consume a trailing ident inside the number arm when a '(' follows - let the generic ident path (cssurl.rs:281-300, which checks for `(` and recognises url) handle it, so `1.url(` yields number, delim, url-function exactly as the browser. Add V4-08 tests (escape, comment/decoy, case/whitespace): the style-attribute and style-body payloads above (comment decoy), `1.url("...` (unterminated-string decoy swallowing a later url), `+1.url(`, `-1.url(`, `.5.url(`, `1.\75rl(/*)` (escaped), each with the later real url reported Denied(ExternalScheme); keep the `1url(` dimension case as a non-report.

new_findings.kind: security (documented/accepted limitation that can still hide a browser-loaded URL)
new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-web/src/lib.rs:43 DESCRIPTOR assets.not_scanned ('image-set() and src() string arguments'); cssurl.rs css_references (only url( functions and @import are recognised)
new_findings.evidence: A CSS `image-set()` / `-webkit-image-set()` (and the `src()` function) with a BARE STRING argument - `background:image-set("https://evil.example/x.png" 1x)` - loads that URL in a browser, but css_references reports only `url(` tokens and `@import` strings, so a bare-string image-set URL is not classified (no Denied, no port call). image-set with a nested `url("...")` IS caught (css_references finds the url token). This is listed in not_scanned and was accepted at R5; it is unchanged since the R7 PASS, so it is a pre-existing documented limitation, not a new regression - raised so the lead can decide whether a bare-string image-set / src() URL should be classified rather than silently not scanned.
new_findings.remediation: Optional: recognise the string argument of image-set()/-webkit-image-set()/src() as a URL (Denied/port like url()), or keep the documented limitation if out of scope. Not required to clear R10-F1.

lanes.adversarial_text_consumer_scan: Per the R9 root-cause rule (every text consumer reads the parser's text, raw spans only locate): attribute values -> charref::decode(Attribute) (preprocessing, U+0000, references); names -> local_name/attr_local_name (name_key); text/RCDATA/foreign CDATA -> text_value; RAWTEXT/script -> raw_text_data; comments -> comment_value; HTML & foreign style -> sheet()/stylesheet_text. href/xlink:href, src, poster, object data/codebase/classid/archive, form action, formaction, cite, ping, srcset/imagesrcset, background/longdesc/lowsrc/manifest, meta refresh, base href, SVG presentation attrs, @import and style bodies all route through those decoded texts (V4-06 58-site list re-verified). iframe srcdoc is Denied(InlineDocument) and its contents are not scanned (by design). The one place the crate's reading still diverges from a browser's is the CSS TOKENISER itself (R10-F1), not the raw-vs-parser-text boundary. The @import and url() paths decode CSS escapes, treat comments and strings as tokens, and handle CR/LF/FF as url whitespace correctly; the hole is the number-prefix mis-tokenisation only. No other consumer found reading raw source where browser text is required.
lanes.normalised_text_rule_check: Sound. sheet() concatenates text_value of each text/CDATA child (foreign) or raw_text_data (HTML) - the parser's character data; stylesheet_text exposes it; preview (preview.rs:340-342) and media blocks (responsive.rs:363-368) read the same sheet with its span map. WebDoc::stylesheet_text span mapping (Sheet::span, dom.rs:350-357 + CharData::span): exact for an HTML style body or a single foreign piece (map = CharData, one mark per CR LF / U+0000, capped at max_nodes then falls back to the whole content span - V4-01/02 bounded), and the whole content span when pieces are concatenated. V4-01: the map is bounded (max_marks); no allocation sized from declared values.
lanes.d9_table_check: Every detection-rule row (construction.rs module docs, 13.2.6.4 rows) has at least one refusing input in tree_construction_that_moves_authored_nodes_is_refused_typed, including the arms R9 review B named (rb/rtc, option-with-select, optgroup-without-select) and the text rows (colgroup text, head-noscript text). End-tag rows checked: the crate keeps only the current node's own end tag (pops exactly that node in every listed mode), </image> (ignored except in colgroup = F2 refused, and after </body>/</html> = refused), and </> (no token). Verified against the spec that 13.2.6.4.7 'pre/listing/textarea' ignore the next LF token and 13.2.5.7 </> emits none, so the first-LF and colgroup handling are spec-correct.
lanes.oracle_correction_O1_check: Justified by the spec and hides no crate defect. WHATWG 13.2.5.7 (U+003E: parse error, switch to data state, emits no token) and 13.2.6 ('the next token ... even if subsequently just ignored') confirm </> produces no token, so 13.2.6.4.7's 'if the next token is an LF' sees the LF after <pre></>. html5ever 0.40.1 instead clears the ignore-LF flag on the parse-error token (tree_builder/mod.rs:481), keeping the LF - a genuine html5ever deviation. harness.rs oracle_input (:35-68) removes </> from the html5ever REFERENCE input only where the tokenizer is in the data state with nothing pending (span.start==0 or the preceding byte is '>'), leaving </> after '<'/'&' and inside scripting-on noscript RAWTEXT. The crate's own first-LF behaviour is pinned against the spec by end_tag_open_without_name_emits_no_token, independent of html5ever, so the correction cannot mask a crate defect.
